messages.subject: Priors for spatial lengthscale
parts:
I'm trying to model the mean values of data collected from a number of sites where means at each site can be spatially autocorrelated.  I used a squared-exponential covariance function to build the spatial correlation matrix.Unfortunately, the model has a large number of diverging errors; it also fails with the cholesky decomposition of the matrix frequently enough for me to think that it's a substantial problem.  (Message: "Exception thrown at line 36: cholesky_decompose: Cholesky decomposition of m failed")

This model has no difficulties if the spatial component is removed. I think the most likely source of the error would be the prior for the spatial lengthscale.  I'd like for this parameter to be able to shrink to near-0 (which result in an identity matrix for the spatial correlation) while still having sufficient mass in the tail to allow for substantial spatial signal.  I've tried a variety of options (half Cauchy, half student_t, exponential), but none seem to have improved anything. 

Is there something else wrong with this model?  Should I be using a different covariance function? Does anyone have any suggestions or advice for the prior?

Thank you

/* Model Objectives:
Estimate the mean value at each site and the grand mean.
Allow for standard deviation to vary among sites
Account for spatial autocorrelation of means among sites
*/
data{
  int n; // observations
  int nSite; // sites
  int siteID[n]; // which site belongs to each obs. 
  vector[n] x;
  matrix[nSite,nSite] Dist; // Distance matrix, pre-scaled so the minimum distance is 1
}
transformed data{
  real xScale; // the range of x divided by 4, to establish a reasonable scale for priors
  real xMean;
  matrix[nSite,nSite] sqDist; // pre-compute squared distance matrix
  xMean <- mean(x);
  xScale <- (max(x) - min(x))/4;
  for(i in 1:nSite) for(j in 1:nSite)
    sqDist[i,j] <- Dist[i,j]^2;
}
parameters{
  real<lower=0> spatialScale; // spatial lengthscale; 
  real grandMean; // overall mean of x
  
  // Non-central parameterizations; use is defined in next block
  vector[nSite] raw_siteMean;
  real<lower=0,upper=pi()/2> raw_siteSD;
  real<lower=0,upper=pi()/2> raw_indSDHier;
  vector<lower=0,upper=pi()/2>[nSite] raw_indSD;
}
transformed parameters{
  vector[nSite] siteMean; // mean of x at each site
  real siteSD; // stdev of siteMean
  real indSDHier; // overall stdev of x around the sitemeans
  vector[nSite] indSD; // each site's scaling of indSDHier
  
  matrix[nSite, nSite] Sigma_spatial; // Spatial matrix
  matrix[nSite,nSite] L_Sigma_spatial; // cholesky of spatial matrix
  Sigma_spatial <- exp(-sqDist/(2*spatialScale^2)); // squared exponential covariance
  L_Sigma_spatial <- cholesky_decompose(Sigma_spatial);
  
  siteSD <- tan(raw_siteSD) * xScale; // ~half-cauchy(0, xScale)
  siteMean <-  siteSD * 
    L_Sigma_spatial * // comment out this line to remove spatial dependence
    raw_siteMean + grandMean; // ~ MVN_chol(grandMean, siteSD*L_Sigma_spatial); 
  indSDHier <- tan(raw_indSDHier) * xScale; // ~half-cauchy(0, xScale)
  for(i in 1:nSite)
    indSD[i] <- indSDHier * tan(raw_indSD[i]); // ~half-cauchy(0, indSDHier)
}
model{
  grandMean ~ normal(xMean,xScale);
  raw_siteMean ~ normal(0,1);
  spatialScale  ~ cauchy(0, 1); // A variety of other priors have been attempted, including student_t and exponential
  x ~ normal(siteMean[siteID], indSD[siteID]);
}
 

If it helps, I can provide some data and a set-up script. This was all run in rstan 2.9.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Priors for spatial lengthscale
parts:
The length scale shrinking to zero does not give
you an identity covariance but rather a covariance
where all entries are unity, which is not positive-definite
and hence will frustrate the Cholesky decomposition.

A prior will still be helpful, but you really need to add
a multiple of the identity matrix, with the scaling another
possible parameter, to Sigma_spatial to regularize the
covariance.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Priors for spatial lengthscale
parts:
Christopher, have you tried using an inverse-lengthscale parameterization? You simply change this:

    Sigma_spatial <- exp(-sqDist/(2*spatialScale^2)); 

to

    Sigma_spatial <- exp(-sqDist*(2*spatialScale^2)); 

I find this a more intuitive parameterization as values from 0-1 imply near-monotonicity within the range of the data (if x is scaled to 0-1), making the typical peaked-at-zero priors sensibly reflecting a bias for simpler functions. 


--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

On Wed, Jun 22, 2016, at 09:58 PM, Mike Lawrence wrote:
> Christopher, have you tried using an inverse-lengthscale
> parameterization?
> You simply change this:
>
>     Sigma_spatial <- exp(-sqDist/(2*spatialScale^2));
>
> to
>
>     Sigma_spatial <- exp(-sqDist*(2*spatialScale^2));
>
> I find this a more intuitive parameterization as values from 0-1 imply
> near-monotonicity within the range of the data (if x is scaled to 0-1),
> making the typical peaked-at-zero priors sensibly reflecting a bias for
> simpler functions.
>
>
> --
> Mike Lawrence
> Graduate Student
> Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
> Dalhousie University
>
> ~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~
>
>
> On Tue, Jun 21, 2016 at 6:12 PM, Michael Betancourt
> <betan...@gmail.com>
> wrote:
>
> > The length scale shrinking to zero does not give
> > you an identity covariance but rather a covariance
> > where all entries are unity, which is not positive-definite
> > and hence will frustrate the Cholesky decomposition.
> >
> > A prior will still be helpful, but you really need to add
> > a multiple of the identity matrix, with the scaling another
> > possible parameter, to Sigma_spatial to regularize the
> > covariance.
> >
> > On Jun 21, 2016, at 9:07 PM, Christopher Peterson <
> > chr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > I'm trying to model the mean values of data collected from a number of
> > sites where means at each site can be spatially autocorrelated.  I used a
> > squared-exponential covariance function to build the spatial correlation
> > matrix.Unfortunately, the model has a large number of diverging errors; it
> > also fails with the cholesky decomposition of the matrix frequently enough
> > for me to think that it's a substantial problem.
> >
> > This model has no difficulties if the spatial component is removed. I
> > think the most likely source of the error would be the prior for the
> > spatial lengthscale.  I'd like for this parameter to be able to shrink to
> > near-0 (which result in an identity matrix for the spatial correlation)
> > while still having sufficient mass in the tail to allow for substantial
> > spatial signal.  I've tried a variety of options (half Cauchy, half
> > student_t, exponential), but none seem to have improved anything.
> >
> > Is there something else wrong with this model?  Should I be using a
> > different covariance function? Does anyone have any suggestions or advice
> > for the prior?
> >
> > Thank you
> >
> > /* Model Objectives:
> > Estimate the mean value at each site and the grand mean.
> > Allow for standard deviation to vary among sites
> > Account for spatial autocorrelation of means among sites
> > */
> > data{
> >   int n; // observations
> >   int nSite; // sites
> >   int siteID[n]; // which site belongs to each obs.
> >   vector[n] x;
> >   matrix[nSite,nSite] Dist; // Distance matrix, pre-scaled so the minimum
> > distance is 1
> > }
> > transformed data{
> >   real xScale; // the range of x divided by 4, to establish a reasonable
> > scale for priors
> >   real xMean;
> >   matrix[nSite,nSite] sqDist; // pre-compute squared distance matrix
> >   xMean <- mean(x);
> >   xScale <- (max(x) - min(x))/4;
> >   for(i in 1:nSite) for(j in 1:nSite)
> >     sqDist[i,j] <- Dist[i,j]^2;
> > }
> > parameters{
> >   real<lower=0> spatialScale; // spatial lengthscale;
> >   real grandMean; // overall mean of x
> >
> >   // Non-central parameterizations; use is defined in next block
> >   vector[nSite] raw_siteMean;
> >   real<lower=0,upper=pi()/2> raw_siteSD;
> >   real<lower=0,upper=pi()/2> raw_indSDHier;
> >   vector<lower=0,upper=pi()/2>[nSite] raw_indSD;
> > }
> > transformed parameters{
> >   vector[nSite] siteMean; // mean of x at each site
> >   real siteSD; // stdev of siteMean
> >   real indSDHier; // overall stdev of x around the sitemeans
> >   vector[nSite] indSD; // each site's scaling of indSDHier
> >
> >   matrix[nSite, nSite] Sigma_spatial; // Spatial matrix
> >   matrix[nSite,nSite] L_Sigma_spatial; // cholesky of spatial matrix
> >   Sigma_spatial <- exp(-sqDist/(2*spatialScale^2)); // squared exponential
> > covariance
> >   L_Sigma_spatial <- cholesky_decompose(Sigma_spatial);
> >
> >   siteSD <- tan(raw_siteSD) * xScale; // ~half-cauchy(0, xScale)
> >   siteMean <-  siteSD *
> >     L_Sigma_spatial * // comment out this line to remove spatial dependence
> >     raw_siteMean + grandMean; // ~ MVN_chol(grandMean,
> > siteSD*L_Sigma_spatial);
> >   indSDHier <- tan(raw_indSDHier) * xScale; // ~half-cauchy(0, xScale)
> >   for(i in 1:nSite)
> >     indSD[i] <- indSDHier * tan(raw_indSD[i]); // ~half-cauchy(0,
> > indSDHier)
> > }
> > model{
> >   grandMean ~ normal(xMean,xScale);
> >   raw_siteMean ~ normal(0,1);
> >   spatialScale  ~ cauchy(0, 1); // A variety of other priors have been
> > attempted, including student_t and exponential
> >   x ~ normal(siteMean[siteID], indSD[siteID]);
> > }
> >
> >

> >

messages.author: fa6f5d4c13c0cca5
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Priors for spatial lengthscale
parts:
Regarding the original question:

I'm a bit confused as to how that would work.  Given the squared-exponential covariance function Cov[i,j] = sigma^2 * exp(-D[i,j]^2 / l^2), where D[i,j] is the fixed distance between points i and j and l is the length-scale parameter, I was under the impression that as l^2 approached 0,  exp(-D[i,j]^2 / l^2) would also approach 0 for the off-diagonals (while the diagonals, with 0 distance, remained at 1).  Thus, a prior that shrunk l towards 0 should reduce the correlation to an identity matrix.  Is this mistaken?  I know I must be screwing something up somewhere, but I don't see how this is it. 

Thank you for your help, everyone.

On Tuesday, June 21, 2016 at 5:12:24 PM UTC-4, Michael Betancourt wrote:
The length scale shrinking to zero does not give
you an identity covariance but rather a covariance
where all entries are unity, which is not positive-definite
and hence will frustrate the Cholesky decomposition.

A prior will still be helpful, but you really need to add
a multiple of the identity matrix, with the scaling another
possible parameter, to Sigma_spatial to regularize the
covariance.

On Jun 21, 2016, at 9:07 PM, Christopher Peterson <christopher...@gmail.com> wrote:

I'm trying to model the mean values of data collected from a number of sites where means at each site can be spatially autocorrelated.  I used a squared-exponential covariance function to build the spatial correlation matrix.Unfortunately, the model has a large number of diverging errors; it also fails with the cholesky decomposition of the matrix frequently enough for me to think that it's a substantial problem.  

This model has no difficulties if the spatial component is removed. I think the most likely source of the error would be the prior for the spatial lengthscale.  I'd like for this parameter to be able to shrink to near-0 (which result in an identity matrix for the spatial correlation) while still having sufficient mass in the tail to allow for substantial spatial signal.  I've tried a variety of options (half Cauchy, half student_t, exponential), but none seem to have improved anything. 

Is there something else wrong with this model?  Should I be using a different covariance function? Does anyone have any suggestions or advice for the prior?

Thank you

/* Model Objectives:
Estimate the mean value at each site and the grand mean.
Allow for standard deviation to vary among sites
Account for spatial autocorrelation of means among sites
*/
data{
  int n; // observations
  int nSite; // sites
  int siteID[n]; // which site belongs to each obs. 
  vector[n] x;
  matrix[nSite,nSite] Dist; // Distance matrix, pre-scaled so the minimum distance is 1
}
transformed data{
  real xScale; // the range of x divided by 4, to establish a reasonable scale for priors
  real xMean;
  matrix[nSite,nSite] sqDist; // pre-compute squared distance matrix
  xMean <- mean(x);
  xScale <- (max(x) - min(x))/4;
  for(i in 1:nSite) for(j in 1:nSite)
    sqDist[i,j] <- Dist[i,j]^2;
}
parameters{
  real<lower=0> spatialScale; // spatial lengthscale; 
  real grandMean; // overall mean of x
  
  // Non-central parameterizations; use is defined in next block
  vector[nSite] raw_siteMean;
  real<lower=0,upper=pi()/2> raw_siteSD;
  real<lower=0,upper=pi()/2> raw_indSDHier;
  vector<lower=0,upper=pi()/2>[nSite] raw_indSD;
}
transformed parameters{
  vector[nSite] siteMean; // mean of x at each site
  real siteSD; // stdev of siteMean
  real indSDHier; // overall stdev of x around the sitemeans
  vector[nSite] indSD; // each site's scaling of indSDHier
  
  matrix[nSite, nSite] Sigma_spatial; // Spatial matrix
  matrix[nSite,nSite] L_Sigma_spatial; // cholesky of spatial matrix
  Sigma_spatial <- exp(-sqDist/(2*spatialScale^2)); // squared exponential covariance
  L_Sigma_spatial <- cholesky_decompose(Sigma_spatial);
  
  siteSD <- tan(raw_siteSD) * xScale; // ~half-cauchy(0, xScale)
  siteMean <-  siteSD * 
    L_Sigma_spatial * // comment out this line to remove spatial dependence
    raw_siteMean + grandMean; // ~ MVN_chol(grandMean, siteSD*L_Sigma_spatial); 
  indSDHier <- tan(raw_indSDHier) * xScale; // ~half-cauchy(0, xScale)
  for(i in 1:nSite)
    indSD[i] <- indSDHier * tan(raw_indSD[i]); // ~half-cauchy(0, indSDHier)
}
model{
  grandMean ~ normal(xMean,xScale);
  raw_siteMean ~ normal(0,1);
  spatialScale  ~ cauchy(0, 1); // A variety of other priors have been attempted, including student_t and exponential
  x ~ normal(siteMean[siteID], indSD[siteID]);
}
 

If it helps, I can provide some data and a set-up script.

Here's some R code to help intuition:

  library(MASS)
  inv_rho = .001 #contrast .001 & 10
  eta = 1
  sigma = 1
  N = 1e2
  s = matrix(NA,nrow=N,ncol=N)
  for(i in 1:N){
    for(j in 1:N){
      s[i, j] = eta * exp(-((i-j)^2)*inv_rho) + sigma
    }
  }
  out = MASS::mvrnorm(1,rep(0,times=N),s)
  plot(out,type='l',ylim=c(-10,10))

As has been pointed out in other threads here, inv_rho & eta play somewhat similar roles in areas of the parameter space, but generally you should observe that for a given value of eta, you get more wiggly plots with larger values for inv_rho.

On Thu, Jun 23, 2016 at 8:12 PM, Christopher Peterson <christopher...@gmail.com> wrote:

Regarding the original question:

I'm a bit confused as to how that would work.  Given the squared-exponential covariance function Cov[i,j] = sigma^2 * exp(-D[i,j]^2 / l^2), where D[i,j] is the fixed distance between points i and j and l is the length-scale parameter, I was under the impression that as l^2 approached 0,  exp(-D[i,j]^2 / l^2) would also approach 0 for the off-diagonals (while the diagonals, with 0 distance, remained at 1).  Thus, a prior that shrunk l towards 0 should reduce the correlation to an identity matrix.  Is this mistaken?  I know I must be screwing something up somewhere, but I don't see how this is it. 

Thank you for your help, everyone.

On Tuesday, June 21, 2016 at 5:12:24 PM UTC-4, Michael Betancourt wrote:
The length scale shrinking to zero does not give
you an identity covariance but rather a covariance
where all entries are unity, which is not positive-definite
and hence will frustrate the Cholesky decomposition.

A prior will still be helpful, but you really need to add
a multiple of the identity matrix, with the scaling another
possible parameter, to Sigma_spatial to regularize the
covariance.

On Jun 21, 2016, at 9:07 PM, Christopher Peterson <christopher...@gmail.com> wrote:

I'm trying to model the mean values of data collected from a number of sites where means at each site can be spatially autocorrelated.  I used a squared-exponential covariance function to build the spatial correlation matrix.Unfortunately, the model has a large number of diverging errors; it also fails with the cholesky decomposition of the matrix frequently enough for me to think that it's a substantial problem.  

This model has no difficulties if the spatial component is removed. I think the most likely source of the error would be the prior for the spatial lengthscale.  I'd like for this parameter to be able to shrink to near-0 (which result in an identity matrix for the spatial correlation) while still having sufficient mass in the tail to allow for substantial spatial signal.  I've tried a variety of options (half Cauchy, half student_t, exponential), but none seem to have improved anything. 

Is there something else wrong with this model?  Should I be using a different covariance function? Does anyone have any suggestions or advice for the prior?

Thank you

/* Model Objectives:
Estimate the mean value at each site and the grand mean.
Allow for standard deviation to vary among sites
Account for spatial autocorrelation of means among sites
*/

  int n; // observations
  int nSite; // sites
  int siteID[n]; // which site belongs to each obs. 
  vector[n] x;
  matrix[nSite,nSite] Dist; // Distance matrix, pre-scaled so the minimum distance is 1
}
transformed data{
  real xScale; // the range of x divided by 4, to establish a reasonable scale for priors
  real xMean;
  matrix[nSite,nSite] sqDist; // pre-compute squared distance matrix
  xMean <- mean(x);
  xScale <- (max(x) - min(x))/4;
  for(i in 1:nSite) for(j in 1:nSite)
    sqDist[i,j] <- Dist[i,j]^2;
}
parameters{
  real<lower=0> spatialScale; // spatial lengthscale; 
  real grandMean; // overall mean of x
  
  // Non-central parameterizations; use is defined in next block
  vector[nSite] raw_siteMean;
  real<lower=0,upper=pi()/2> raw_siteSD;
  real<lower=0,upper=pi()/2> raw_indSDHier;
  vector<lower=0,upper=pi()/2>[nSite] raw_indSD;
}
transformed parameters{
  vector[nSite] siteMean; // mean of x at each site
  real siteSD; // stdev of siteMean
  real indSDHier; // overall stdev of x around the sitemeans
  vector[nSite] indSD; // each site's scaling of indSDHier
  
  matrix[nSite, nSite] Sigma_spatial; // Spatial matrix
  matrix[nSite,nSite] L_Sigma_spatial; // cholesky of spatial matrix
  Sigma_spatial <- exp(-sqDist/(2*spatialScale^2)); // squared exponential covariance
  L_Sigma_spatial <- cholesky_decompose(Sigma_spatial);
  
  siteSD <- tan(raw_siteSD) * xScale; // ~half-cauchy(0, xScale)
  siteMean <-  siteSD * 
    L_Sigma_spatial * // comment out this line to remove spatial dependence
    raw_siteMean + grandMean; // ~ MVN_chol(grandMean, siteSD*L_Sigma_spatial); 
  indSDHier <- tan(raw_indSDHier) * xScale; // ~half-cauchy(0, xScale)
  for(i in 1:nSite)
    indSD[i] <- indSDHier * tan(raw_indSD[i]); // ~half-cauchy(0, indSDHier)
}
model{
  grandMean ~ normal(xMean,xScale);
  raw_siteMean ~ normal(0,1);
  spatialScale  ~ cauchy(0, 1); // A variety of other priors have been attempted, including student_t and exponential
  x ~ normal(siteMean[siteID], indSD[siteID]);
}

I think that informative priors on lenghscale can make a lot of sense.  To start with:  at the extremes of lengthscales near 0 or infinity, there will be no info to learn about this hyperparameter.  And, a lot of the time, you can get some (soft) bounds on reasonable lenghtscale based on the nature of the problem.  For example if we're modeling annual economic data, we probably wouldn't want a lenghtscale less than 2 years.  And so on.
A
